claims.text: 「調理器具も完全に分けていて、小麦粉の持ち込みは一切禁止」 — cooking equipment is completely separated and bringing wheat flour onto the premises is entirely prohibited.
「小麦はもちろん、大麦、ライ麦、オーツ麦など、グルテンを含む穀物を一切使用しない環境を徹底しています」 — the establishment rigorously maintains an environment free of every gluten grain (wheat, barley, rye, oats).
Caveat noted by coverage: 「一部調味料の製造工場では小麦を扱っている場合があります。重度の小麦アレルギーの方は、来店前にお店へ直接ご確認いただくことをおすすめします」 — some condiment factories may also process wheat, so severe sufferers should confirm directly.
Uses wheat-free tamari soy sauce (グルテンフリー醤油) for marinating and seasoning instead of standard wheat-containing shoyu; seasonings (醤油, 味噌, だし) are verified for wheat content.
No vegan-specific cross-contact protocol is published; the kitchen handles fish, egg and meat, so vegan diners should ask about dashi and fillings.
The owner 'naco' has a severe wheat allergy and personally set up the separated-kitchen, no-wheat-flour operation, so staff understand allergen safety firsthand.
The venue's site states 「厳選された食材と独自の品質管理で、小麦アレルギーの方にも安心してお召し上がりいただけ」 — carefully selected ingredients and proprietary quality management make it safe for those with wheat allergy.
Entirely gluten-free menu — every dish, including fried Nagoya specialties, is made without any gluten grain using rice-flour breading.
Full-service sit-down washoku restaurant (28 seats) a 3-minute walk from Nagoya Station west exit — a genuine celiac-safe full-meal option, not just takeaway.

name: Bakeshop SolSol (グルテンフリー米粉パン専門店 Bakeshop SolSol)

claims.text: Dedicated gluten-free premises — opened as a standalone shop expressly to keep the kitchen separate from wheat bread (「小麦パンと厨房を分けるために、専門店として独立開業しました」).
「全ての商品に小麦を使っていません」— none of the products use wheat (JP celiac guide, ★★★★★).
Bakery — soy sauce is not a core ingredient; wheat is excluded from the shop entirely.
Not a vegan operation; dairy and egg are used in many items. No vegan cross-contact protocol published.
Founded around a family member's wheat allergy; the whole business model is wheat-free allergy safety (「小麦粉アレルギーがある方でも安心して召し上がっていただけます」).
100% wheat-free rice-flour bakery with a purpose-built separate kitchen.
★★★★★ on the Japanese gluten-free guide; award-winning gluten-free campagne.
No wheat is used anywhere in the shop — the entire product range is 乳卵小麦不使用 (no dairy/egg/wheat), so cross-contact with wheat flour is essentially absent.
Sweets shop — no soy-sauce dishes; wheat-based seasonings are not part of the product line.
Fully vegan facility — no dairy, eggs or animal products used, so no animal-product cross-contact.
Owner is a cooking instructor specializing in allergen-free (乳卵小麦不使用) baking; some items are additionally labeled nut-free (※一部ナッツフリー商品).
Every product is both vegan and gluten-free — no wheat, dairy, egg or white sugar used at all.
Uses 米粉 (rice flour) and 大豆粉 (soy flour) as the base for cakes and baked goods.

name: 米粉Cafe 沙羅双樹 (Komeko Cafe Sarasoju)

claims.text: The owner has a wheat allergy herself and built the cafe specifically around gluten-free rice flour, so staff understand wheat avoidance from personal experience.
All bread, cakes and lunch dishes are made from a 100% domestic rice flour blend rather than wheat flour, making this a rare central-Nara cafe where the whole menu is gluten-free by design.
The owner became interested in gluten-free rice flour after developing a wheat allergy and earned rice flour master certification before opening, reflecting genuine expertise in wheat-free baking.

name: ならまちヴィーガン 菜美（nabi） (Naramachi Vegan Nabi)

claims.text: The entire kitchen is wheat-free, buckwheat-free and peanut-free — these allergens are deliberately not used anywhere, so cross-contamination risk from wheat is minimal.
Umami is drawn from kombu, shiitake and vegetable stock rather than wheat-based seasonings, and the kitchen avoids wheat entirely.
All menu items are 100% vegan with no animal products in the kitchen, so vegan cross-contact is not a concern.
Guests with dietary restrictions are explicitly asked to contact the shop in advance so the kitchen can accommodate them.
Every single dish is completely vegan, gluten-free and nut-free, founded specifically to serve people with food allergies.
English-speaking staff and an English menu make it easy to confirm ingredients.
店全体が小麦粉を一切使わない100%グルテンフリー方針のため、店内に小麦を持ち込まない調理体制。専用フライヤーや厳密なセリアック対応の明記はないため、重度のセリアック病の場合は来店時に確認すると安心。
醤油・タレ類の原材料（小麦含有の有無）についてのウェブ上の明記は確認できず。グルテンフリー専門店だがソース類の確認は来店時に行うと確実。
店全体が100%プラントベースで動物性食材を扱わないため、ヴィーガンの交差接触リスクは低い。
「アレルギーをもつ子どもにもケーキを」という理念で創業しており、アレルギー対応への配慮が店のコンセプトの中心。英語スタッフ・英語メニューもあり相談しやすい。
100%プラントベース＆グルテンフリー、無添加・化学調味料不使用で、ヴィーガンもグルテンフリーの旅行者も全メニューから安心して選べる。
卵・乳製品・小麦・動物性食材を一切使わないため、複数のアレルギーを持つ人も同じテーブルで食事を共有できる。

Completely gluten-free bakery that does not bring gluten-containing ingredients into the production site: 「『完全』グルテンフリーのベーカリー…グルテンを含む原材料を生産現場に持ち込まない」. No wheat handled on premises, so cross-contact is eliminated at source.
「小麦を持ち込まない完全グルテンフリー製造工場」 — a completely gluten-free manufacturing facility with no wheat brought in.
Bakery (breads only) — no soy-sauce-based dishes; standard products use 米粉 (rice flour), 米油 (rice oil) and てんさい糖 (beet sugar).
Butter, egg and dairy are used in some items (e.g. 塩バターロール, 豆乳クリームパン, sweet breads), so vegan customers should confirm the specific product; the facility is not vegan-only.
Founder Miyagi Nobuo has a wheat allergy himself and built the business around allergen safety; site names 小麦アレルギー・セリアック病・グルテン不耐性 as who the bakery is safe for.
Explicitly states products are safe for people with wheat allergy, celiac disease and gluten intolerance: 「小麦アレルギー、セリアック病やグルテン不耐性の方でも安心してお召し上がりいただけます」.
100% domestic rice flour, zero wheat flour, in a dedicated wheat-free facility — the gold-standard setup for a celiac.

name: フルール ド サラザン (Fleur de Sarrasin)

claims.text: This is not a dedicated gluten-free facility — some galette fillings and sauces contain gluten, so diners with celiac disease are advised to tell staff in advance and confirm each dish before ordering.
When a customer disclosed having celiac disease, the chef went through the menu and identified which galettes use a soy sauce containing wheat so those could be avoided.

The French-trained owner is described as very knowledgeable about gluten allergies, showing guests the raw buckwheat grain and the in-house stone mill and explaining which items are safe once notified of an allergy.
The galette batter is 100% buckwheat flour, milled fresh in-house every morning, giving the core dish a naturally gluten-free base before any fillings or sauces are added.
